name: Binary Analysis & Reverse Engineering
description: Disassembly, decompilation, binary similarity, and reverse engineering of compiled code.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area was less about pure binary analysis and more about making analysis harder for adversaries, reflecting an obfuscation-versus-deobfuscation arms race. Papers like "Tackling runtime-based obfuscation in Android with TIRO" (2018) and "AntiFuzz: Impeding Fuzzing Audits of Binary Executables" (2019) framed reverse engineering as a battle: malware authors and software vendors hid behavior at runtime or actively impeded fuzzers, and analysts had to claw it back. This theme continued strongly into 2021-2022 with "MBA-Blast: Unveiling and Simplifying Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic Obfuscation" (2021), which cracked a popular obfuscation technique, and "Loki: Hardening Code Obfuscation Against Automated Attacks" (2022), which pushed back by building obfuscation resilient to the very automated attacks researchers had developed.

A major shift arrived as the field embraced machine learning for the foundational, unglamorous problems of binary analysis: disassembly and code understanding. "DeepDi" (2022) used a relational graph convolutional network to make disassembly fast and accurate, while "DeepReflect: Discovering Malicious Functionality through Binary Reconstruction" (2021) applied deep learning to surface malicious behavior. Alongside this enthusiasm came a crucial wave of rigor and self-reflection: "Ground Truth for Binary Disassembly is Not Easy" (2022) questioned whether the field could even reliably evaluate its tools, and "RE-Mind: a First Look Inside the Mind of a Reverse Engineer" (2022) studied the human analyst directly, acknowledging that reverse engineering is a cognitive skill, not just an algorithm.

By 2023-2024 the area matured into two clear fronts. First, learning-based binary analysis tackled harder, more practical problems: "TYGR: Type Inference on Stripped Binaries using Graph Neural Networks" (2024) recovered types from stripped binaries, and "Can a Deep Learning Model for One Architecture Be Used for Others?" (2023) confronted cross-architecture generalization. Second, decompilation itself became a first-class research target with a sharp emphasis on correctness and quality: "Ahoy SAILR!" (2024) rethought control-flow structuring to produce more readable C, "A Taxonomy of C Decompiler Fidelity Issues" (2024) systematized where decompilers go wrong, and "D-Helix: A Generic Decompiler Testing Framework Using Symbolic Differentiation" (2024) built infrastructure to test decompilers automatically.

Taken together, the trajectory runs from an obfuscation arms race, through the injection of deep learning into core disassembly and code-understanding tasks, to a mature phase marked by methodological scrutiny (ground truth, human studies, fidelity taxonomies) and a serious push to make decompilation both correct and usable. The area today balances powerful learned tools against a hard-won awareness of how to evaluate and trust them.

milestones.title: Tackling runtime-based obfuscation in Android with TIRO
milestones.note: early framing of reverse engineering as an arms race against runtime obfuscation in real malware

milestones.title: MBA-Blast: Unveiling and Simplifying Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic Obfuscation
milestones.note: systematically broke a widely used obfuscation technique, advancing automated deobfuscation

milestones.title: DeepDi: Learning a Relational Graph Convolutional Network Model on Instructions for Fast and Accurate Disassembly
milestones.note: brought graph neural networks to the foundational task of disassembly for speed and accuracy

milestones.title: Ground Truth for Binary Disassembly is Not Easy
milestones.note: injected methodological rigor by questioning how the field even validates disassembly tools

milestones.title: Can a Deep Learning Model for One Architecture Be Used for Others? Retargeted-Architecture Binary Code Analysis
milestones.note: confronted cross-architecture generalization, a key practical limit of learned binary models

milestones.title: Ahoy SAILR! There is No Need to DREAM of C: A Compiler-Aware Structuring Algorithm for Binary Decompilation
milestones.note: reframed decompiler success around readable, compiler-aware C output rather than goto elimination

milestones.title: A Taxonomy of C Decompiler Fidelity Issues
milestones.note: systematized where decompilers lose information, defining the quality frontier for the field

milestones.title: TYGR: Type Inference on Stripped Binaries using Graph Neural Networks
milestones.note: applied GNNs to recover types from stripped binaries, a core hard problem in modern RE
